title: Workflows, agents and who owns the control flow

items.stem: In a system that uses a language model, the control flow is the order of steps: which step runs next, and when the system stops. What makes a system an agent rather than a workflow?

options.text: It calls the model more than once to finish one request
The model decides which step or tool comes next and when to stop
It has access to tools such as a booking calendar lookup
It uses a larger model and a longer prompt than a workflow

items.stem: A makerspace assistant's Python code always runs these steps in this order: (1) one model call labels the student's message as 'manual question' or 'booking request'; (2) if it is a booking request, code calls the calendar tool; (3) a second model call writes the reply. The model never chooses a step. What is this system?

options.text: A workflow, because the code fixes the order of steps
An agent, because it uses a model and a tool together
An agent, because the model makes more than one call
A workflow, because it never uses a tool at all

items.stem: Which makerspace task is the best candidate for a fixed workflow instead of an agent?

options.text: Helping a student work out why a laser-cut part keeps burning
Answering any question a student might ask about any machine
Confirming a booking: check the slot, reserve it, send a confirmation
Deciding which of several manuals to search for an unusual problem

items.stem: Assume every model call costs $0.002, whatever its length. For a booking request, a fixed workflow always makes 3 model calls. An agent doing the same job averages 6 model calls, because it decides each step itself. For 500 booking requests, how many more dollars does the agent cost than the workflow?
In one sentence, say who decides what happens next in a workflow and who decides it in an agent.

Your team's budget is small. A student asks, 'My 3D print keeps warping, what should I change?' The right manual pages, and how many lookups are needed, cannot be known in advance. What is the best design for this request?

options.text: A fixed workflow with one search of the printer manual, because it is cheapest
A fixed workflow with exactly five searches, because it is predictable
A fixed workflow, because every part of an assistant should be a workflow
An agent with a step limit, because the number of lookups is open-ended
